answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals account age times honest epochs completed, so a fresh identity starts near zero no matter how many copies exist. Each honest action extends its horizon of accumulated reputation, while any fraud epoch resets the multiplier. Attacking means mass-buying accounts that sit inert for months before they matter, an economic basalt wall of time and fees. Real networks like Sonnet-based agent markets thrive on this because newcomers must earn standing gradually.
